title: Choose Nick’s visual world
question: Which world should make AI-native DX feel unmistakably Nick? The first card is the assigned direction; the others are outside challengers that survived the clarity test.

options.label: The Trace Room
options.lineage: observability traces · systems maps · human evidence
options.thesis: Nick’s work becomes a living trace from practice to proof to workshop.
options.viewport: A large human portrait and AI-native DX thesis anchor the fold while one trace connects current role, shipped work, teaching evidence, and the Workshops destination.
options.risk: Could slip into developer-tool cosplay if traces become terminal chrome; the human portrait and plain-language proof must dominate.

options.label: The Proof Grid
options.lineage: Swiss poster systems · conference programs · documentary fragments
options.thesis: One rigorous grid turns a varied career into calm, undeniable evidence.
options.case: Best raw clarity: technical leaders scan role, work, talks, and workshops instantly, but it identifies Nick less strongly than the assigned world.
options.viewport: An oversized flush-left thesis occupies two-thirds of the grid; portrait, current role, and Workshops action lock into the remaining modules, with proof fragments beginning below.
options.risk: High clarity but easy to become an excellent generic designer portfolio unless Nick’s voice and photography carry the system.

options.label: The Shared Ink Kit
options.lineage: workshop field manuals · three-ink kits · collaborative artifacts
options.thesis: The site feels like the kit a room of practitioners leaves with after the work ships.
options.case: Strongest Nick-specific tactility and workshop connection; it identifies the teaching practice well but needs restraint to avoid repeating the current zine language.
options.viewport: A modern field-manual cover opens into a human portrait, AI-native DX thesis, and one clear Workshops tab; writing and speaking appear as indexed evidence, not stickers.
options.risk: Could regress into cute badges, hard shadows, and nostalgic print effects; geometry must stay precise and contemporary.

options.label: The Live Rundown
options.lineage: split-flap concourses · workshop run-of-show · live system state
options.thesis: Nick’s current work reads as a live rundown: building, teaching, writing, and what departs next.
options.case: Memorable and structurally clear, with natural motion and state; it loses some warmth and risks making the interface more famous than Nick.
options.viewport: A large portrait breaks a disciplined departure board; the active row is Workshops while role, writing, and talks remain legible semantic rows.
options.risk: The conceit can become airport kitsch or motion theater; it must collapse to a calm semantic table under reduced motion.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished technical personal site with a two-column portrait hero, selected work, and a clear workshops button.
canonCard.viewport: Familiar navigation, portrait and thesis side by side, primary workshop action, then selected writing and talks.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand and easy to forget; choose this only if familiarity matters more than a distinctive authored world.
